body.heading: Build your volcano
paragraphs: Stand an empty plastic bottle in the middle of a tray. Build a mountain around it with damp sand, soil, or modelling clay, leaving the bottle top open.
The tray keeps everything tidy. Do this outside or somewhere your adult says a little mess is fine.

body.heading: The eruption
paragraphs: Your adult pours warm water into the bottle until it is about half full, then adds a squirt of washing-up liquid and a few drops of red or orange food colouring.
Now the exciting part: your adult adds two big spoons of bicarbonate of soda, then pours in about half a cup of vinegar. Stand back and watch it fizz and foam over the top.

body.heading: Why it fizzes
paragraphs: Vinegar and bicarbonate of soda do not like staying together. When they mix, they make lots of tiny bubbles of gas.
The bubbles push the foamy liquid up and out, just like pressure pushes lava out of a real volcano, only much slower and cooler in real life.

description: For ages 6–9 with an adult: build a tiny volcano and make it fizz with vinegar and bicarbonate of soda.

safetyNotes: An adult does all the pouring of vinegar and bicarbonate of soda; stand back during the eruption and keep the mixture away from eyes.
Never taste the mixture, and wash hands afterwards; do this outside or on a tray to protect floors.

takeaway: Mixing two kitchen things can make gas, and gas pushes its way out.
